logline: An office worker who hides her face behind an online mask becomes caught in a chain of violent, escalating consequences in this seven-episode noir thriller structured around multiple narrators.

renewal.note: Seven-episode limited series; self-contained narrative based on the Naver webtoon by Mae-mi. No sequel announced.

bollymeter.basis: Structural ambition and a committed ensemble earn it serious consideration; the final stretch loses momentum as it settles into more conventional crime-drama beats.

seasons.review_body: Mask Girl is a structural experiment: seven episodes, each narrated from a different character's perspective, chronicling how one woman's secret online identity triggers a cascade of violence across years. The critical consensus was striking, 100 percent positive across nine Rotten Tomatoes reviews, and Netflix reported 18.5 million views. The praise centered on the show's formal ambition, the way it refuses a single moral protagonist, and Go Hyun-jung's commanding late appearance. The IMDb audience score settled lower at 7.3, reflecting a split between viewers who found the rotating structure exhilarating and those who felt the second half defaulted to genre formula. As a showcase for director Kim Yong-hoon's facility with tone, it remains one of the more formally interesting Korean limited series of 2023.
